headline: Highest risk is data leakage from RD-Agent’s broad network/API access into Whisper’s local-only audio pipeline; prompt injection and capability conflict are low or absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can ingest browser/API content and logs, but Whisper has no clipboard, MCP, filesystem read, or browser surface to consume RD-Agent outputs by default. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff or external orchestration not shown in either profile, so the pathway is weak and requires unusual setup.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies RD-Agent output into Whisper prompts or transcripts, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator feeds RD-Agent text into Whisper as trusted instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows with no manual copy-paste bridge.
Disable any wrapper that forwards RD-Agent text into Whisper prompts.
Use a fixed prompt template for Whisper that ignores external instructions.
Review any orchestration layer for text-to-instruction parsing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent text handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and broad API-backed research data, while Whisper processes audio/speech locally with no network egress. A shared workspace is not documented, but if one exists, RD-Agent’s outputs could expose sensitive material to Whisper workflows; the reverse leak is limited by Whisper’s local-only profile.
conditions: IF RD-Agent and Whisper share a filesystem or workspace, sensitive files may be exposed across the pair.
IF Whisper is wrapped by a service that uploads audio or transcripts elsewhere, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points for the two agents.
Store RD-Agent outputs in a restricted directory.
Avoid placing financial reports or logs in any shared folder.
Confirm Whisper runs without outbound network access.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the orchestrator layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent can support multiple instances and uses APIs/files, but Whisper cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; only read/write contention through an undocumented shared directory would remain, so the overlap is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by an external wrapper, file contention can occur.
IF RD-Agent is configured to write logs into a shared path, collisions become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories to each agent.
Keep Whisper read-only with respect to any shared artifacts.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same git repository.
Serialize any shared file updates through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can generate research outputs and logs, but Whisper is a speech model with no action-taking authority, no browser, and no network egress. Since Whisper does not appear to execute downstream actions based on RD-Agent output, the cascade is limited unless an external orchestrator treats RD-Agent text as authoritative.
conditions: IF an external pipeline feeds RD-Agent text into Whisper as ground truth for transcription or labeling, errors can propagate.
IF a wrapper uses Whisper output to trigger actions outside the profiles, cascading impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between RD-Agent and Whisper outputs.
Require source citations for any RD-Agent-generated claims before reuse.
Do not auto-act on Whisper outputs derived from RD-Agent text.
Log provenance for all cross-agent inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the orchestrator.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, while Whisper handles audio/speech and has no stated residency or retention controls. The pair creates a compliance gap if regulated data is routed through RD-Agent and then into Whisper-derived transcripts or logs; the profiles do not show matching controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is transcribed into Whisper outputs, retention and residency obligations may be implicated.
IF the deployment stores RD-Agent logs and Whisper transcripts under different policies, mismatch risk exists.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of Whisper transcripts where possible.
Align retention settings for logs and transcripts.
Document residency for any hosted RD-Agent APIs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
